facts.fact_text: On 20 April 2013 the applicant participated in a protest against a construction project in a public park in Kyiv.
On 16 August 2013 the applicant entered the Kyiv City Council premises, relying on his status as a journalist and an assistant to a council member.
About an hour after the protest began on 20 April 2013, a police officer approached the applicant and ordered him to get into a police car, allegedly without explanations.
After the applicant refused to comply with the police officer's order to get into a police car, he was handcuffed and brought to the local police station.

The police drew up a report stating that the applicant had maliciously disobeyed a lawful police order, which is an administrative offence under Article 185 of the Code of Administrative Offences, by refusing to go to a police car.
The police report stated that the applicant had grabbed hold of the officer's clothing and tried to throw himself to the ground.
On 18 July 2013 the Obolonskyy Kyiv District Court found the applicant guilty as charged of maliciously disobeying a lawful police order under Article 185 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Obolonskyy Kyiv District Court fined the applicant 255 Ukrainian hryvnias.
On 16 August 2013 the Kyiv Shevchenkivskyy District Court found the applicant guilty of maliciously disobeying a lawful police order in respect of the incident at the Kyiv City Council premises.
The Kyiv Shevchenkivskyy District Court sentenced the applicant to five days' detention for maliciously disobeying a lawful police order on 16 August 2013.
The applicant began serving the five-day detention sentence immediately on 16 August 2013.

In addition to the police report, the Obolonskyy Kyiv District Court relied on the statements of several guards of the construction site who submitted that an aggressive looking group from among the protesters had approached the site, had damaged some equipment and had left.
The applicant stated in the police report that he had not received any lawful orders from police officers.
The applicant stated in the police report that witnesses P. and Ch., who had witnessed his arrest, could confirm his version of the events.
The applicant complained in his appeal that the Obolonskyy Kyiv District Court had arbitrarily rejected his request for questioning witnesses P. and Ch.
On 5 September 2013 the Kyiv City Court of Appeal rejected the applicant's appeal against the Obolonskyy Kyiv District Court's judgment, with reasoning similar to that of the first-instance court.
The Kyiv City Court of Appeal neither commented on the applicant's request for questioning witnesses P. and Ch. nor indicated the reasons for its rejection of that request.
